extName.description: Extension name shown in Chrome Web Store and toolbar.

extDescription.message: Your browsing sessions, reimagined as an interactive graph.
extDescription.description: Short description shown under the extension name.

openTrail.description: Tooltip on the toolbar action icon.

welcome.title: Every click becomes a node.
welcome.body: Trail turns your browsing into a map you can revisit, rearrange, and understand.

privacy.title: We see less than you think.
privacy.body: Trail records just enough to draw the map. Nothing stored leaves your device — unless you opt in to cloud sync later.
privacy.footer: Local-first by default. Cloud sync is opt-in.

branch.title: Backtracking doesn't lose your work.
branch.body: Revisit a page, click a new link — Trail branches so you keep both paths.
branch.footnote: Quick glances fade on their own. If you return, they reappear.

start.title: Start with something real, or start empty.
start.body: Either works. You can always switch trees later.
start.demoBody: ~25 nodes you can pan, collapse, and edit.
start.freshBody: Your next click becomes the first node.
start.footnote: Your current tree (if any) stays saved — you can switch back from the sidepanel.

ready.title: You're set.
ready.body: A few shortcuts to make it feel yours.

hook.title: Never lose a tab again.
hook.body: Trail turns every click into a node you can return to — weeks later, with two letters.

questions.q1: Wait — where was that tab I just had?
questions.q2: How did I end up on this page?
questions.q3: I hit back. Now it's gone.

persona.title: What do you lose in your browser?
persona.subtitle: Pick whichever feels most like you.

research.title: Research threads
research.body: I compare five things at once and get lost.

article.title: That one article
article.body: I meant to come back. I didn't.

learning.title: Learning paths
learning.body: I was deep in something. Now it's gone.

tabs.title: Open tabs
tabs.body: I keep tabs open because I'm scared to close them.

research.title: Every path you explored, kept.
research.body: Click back, try another — both are saved. Nothing dies when you change your mind.
research.imagine: You compare five laptops. Hop between them. Close every tab. Next Tuesday, every path is still there, side by side.

article.title: Every click, a searchable node.
article.body: That thing from Tuesday is two letters away.
article.imagine: You half-read an article at 11pm. Close the tab. Friday afternoon, type two words — it's right there.

learning.title: Your learning is a tree, not a list.
learning.body: Trail draws the tree so you can pick up where you left off.
learning.imagine: You're deep in a React rabbit hole. Life happens. You come back — the exact branch you were on is right where you left it.

tabs.title: Close tabs. Keep them addressable.
tabs.body: Open any node from yesterday like it's still a tab.
tabs.imagine: 40 tabs down to 4. Everything else lives in the graph — one click and you're back in it.

bullets.b1: Every tab you open is a node you can return to.
bullets.b2: Go back, then click somewhere else? Both paths are saved.
bullets.b3: Search what you actually did, not just URLs you typed.

tour.confirmSkip: Exit the tour? Your tour tree will be deleted.

arm.title: Open any site.
arm.body: A news front page, a blog, GitHub, Wikipedia — anything with links. I'll watch the tree start.

clickResult.title: Nice. Click any link on that page.
clickResult.body: Whatever looks interesting. We'll use it as the starting point.

goBack.title: Now press Back.
goBack.body: Go back to the page you came from. Your first click stays saved in the tree.

clickAnother.title: Good. Now click a different link.
clickAnother.body: Pick any other link on the same page. That's where Trail does the interesting part.

celebrateBranch.title: You branched.
celebrateBranch.body: Both paths are saved. Neither disappears when you change your mind.

returnToAbandoned.title: One more — click the highlighted node.
returnToAbandoned.body: See the ring in the graph? That's the first result you opened. Click it here to jump back.

celebration.title: $1 nodes in $2 seconds.
celebration.body: This is what every browsing session could look like.

bodyByPersona.research: Your real research looks just like this — only longer.
bodyByPersona.article: Every article you meant to reread is findable now.
bodyByPersona.learning: Next time a thread resumes, you'll pick up right here.
bodyByPersona.tabs: You can close every one of them. Nothing gets lost.

taglines.research: Your research deserves to outlive this tab.
taglines.article: That article will still be here tomorrow.
taglines.learning: Pick up where you left off — from any device.
taglines.tabs: Every tab, every device, still addressable.

resume.title: Tour paused
resume.body: Pick up from where you left off.

signin.title: Sync across devices
signin.body: Sign in to keep your trails on every browser.

pin.title: Pin Trail to your toolbar
pin.body: Click the puzzle piece in your toolbar, then the pin next to Trail. One click to open from anywhere.

trees.title: Trees
trees.description: Create, open, import, and export your trees.

createDialog.title: Create a new tree
createDialog.description: Trees are independent browsing maps. Each tree keeps its own nodes and history.

deleteDialog.title: Delete "$1"?
deleteDialog.description: This permanently deletes the tree and all its nodes. This cannot be undone.

sync.cloudOnlyTooltip: Cloud only — click to download to this device
sync.localActiveTooltip: Local only · active tree (open another tree to unload this one)
sync.syncedOfferUnloadTooltip: Synced · $1 · click to remove from this device
sync.syncedOfferUnloadTooltipNoTime: Synced · click to remove from this device
sync.localOfferUploadTooltip: Local only — click to sync to cloud and remove from this device

toast.unloaded: Tree unloaded — kept in the cloud only.

account.title: Account
account.descriptionCloudOff: Cloud sync is not configured in this build.
account.descriptionCloudOn: Sign in to sync your trees across devices. Your data stays on your device until you explicitly sign in.
account.localOnlyAlertBodyPrefix: This build of Trail has no Supabase credentials baked in, so cloud sync, sign-in, and cross-device support are turned off. Everything still works locally — your trees live in
account.notSignedInBody: You're not signed in. Your trees are stored locally only. We never see your password — it's hashed before it leaves your device.

security.title: Security
security.dialogDescription: Choose a new password. You'll stay signed in on this device.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.description: These actions are irreversible. Read each description carefully before you confirm.

clearLocal.name: Clear local data
clearLocal.description: Wipes every tree and tree-related state on this profile (sync queue, undo history, tab restoration). Sign-in, settings, and open browser tabs stay. Cloud data is not touched — signed-in users will see their cloud trees reappear as cloud-only entries after the next sync.
clearLocal.confirmBody: Wipes every tree and tree-related state on this profile. Sign-in, settings, and open browser tabs stay. Cloud data is untouched.

delete.name: Delete account
delete.description: Permanently deletes your Trail account and every tree stored in the cloud. Local data is cleared right away; server-side removal finishes within 30 days. This cannot be undone.
delete.confirmBody: This requests deletion of your account and all cloud-stored trees. Local data is cleared immediately. Server-side deletion completes within 30 days per our Privacy Policy. This cannot be undone.

toast.cleared: Local trees cleared. Your browser tabs are untouched.
toast.deletionBody: Your local data has been cleared and your session ended. Server-side data removal completes within 30 days.

feedback.contactPlaceholder: Email or @handle if you'd like a reply
feedback.toastSuccessSentry: Your report was attached to our crash dashboard.

bug.title: Report a bug
bug.description: Tell us what went wrong. If a recent crash was captured, we'll attach it automatically.
bug.placeholder: What happened? What did you expect?

feature.title: Suggest a feature
feature.description: What would make Trail better for you?
feature.placeholder: Describe the feature you'd like to see…

support.title: Contact support
support.description: Stuck on something? We'll get back to you.

login.signupOtpSent: We sent a 6-digit code to your email. Enter it below to finish.
login.recoveryOtpSent: We sent a recovery code to your email. Enter it below, then choose a new password.
login.recoveryCodeAccepted: Code accepted. Choose a new password to finish.
login.signedInDescription: You're signed in. Your trees will start syncing across devices automatically. Open Trail from the extension icon in your toolbar.
login.cloudUnconfiguredDescription: This build of Trail has no Supabase credentials baked in. Sign-in is disabled — your trees still work locally.
